questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a Trailhead Playground, structurally?
options: A free Developer Edition org, created and managed through Trailhead
A copy of a company's real production org
A paid Enterprise Edition subscription
A read-only demo with no Setup access
questions.explain: A Trailhead Playground is a Developer Edition org under the hood, just created and managed through Trailhead's own flow.

questions.q: What is the one distinction this lesson says actually matters between a sandbox and a Trailhead Playground or Developer Edition org?
options: Where the data comes from: a sandbox starts as a copy of a real company's production org, while the other two start empty and belong to you personally
Only sandboxes allow Setup access
Only a Developer Edition org can run Flow
Sandboxes are always more expensive than Trailhead Playgrounds
questions.explain: The core distinction is data origin: a sandbox is a copy of a specific company's production org, while a Playground or Developer Edition org starts empty and belongs to the individual.

questions.q: Can anyone just "create a sandbox" the same way they create a Trailhead Playground, per this lesson?
options: No — a sandbox only exists in relation to a company's paid production org, and requires admin access to that org to create
Yes, anyone can create a sandbox for free at any time with no org attached
Yes, but only Trailhead account holders can create sandboxes
No, sandboxes were discontinued by Salesforce
questions.explain: A sandbox only exists in relation to a specific company's production org and requires admin access to that org to create.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about how Setup, Object Manager, and Flow behave across a Playground, a Developer Edition org, and a sandbox?
options: They look and behave identically across all three environments
They are completely different interfaces in each environment
Flow only exists in sandboxes, never in a Playground
Object Manager is disabled in Developer Edition orgs
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that Setup, Object Manager, and Flow look and work identically across all three, so practice transfers directly.

questions.q: Which environment does this lesson say you'll typically be given once you're working as an admin for a real company?
options: A sandbox of that company's real production org
A brand-new personal Trailhead Playground
Direct, unrestricted admin access to production with no testing environment
A Developer Edition org owned by Salesforce support
questions.explain: Real companies give admins a sandbox of their actual production org to build and test in before changes go live.
